title: The number chart window (`chartwindow`) and its band to 120 (build-list `chart_120`)

template.also: Generator `js/modules/gen-counting.js` (the hundreds_chart_fill / number_chart_fill branch and `_chartGaps`), provider `js/modules/sheet/providers/k2.js` (`chartSteps`, the two `registerSkill` blocks), options `js/modules/skill-options.js` (`_gridOptions`, the P11 block and the `_ap1Put` band of hundreds_chart_fill, `SKILL_OPTIONS['composing:number_chart_fill']`). `screen-cell.js` (`wireChartSwipe`, `fitTwinRows`) and `css/screen-cell.css` draw the same cell on the practice card, online worksheet and quiz

summary: A window cut from a number chart, rows of ten (across is one more, down is ten more), with one to seven empty squares the pupil writes in. Each empty square is a whole chart square with a 1.5 pt border: the writing place. This card signs the template as it stands and the one change the build list asks of it: `chart_120`, a band 120 on composing:hundreds_chart_fill whose window always crosses 100 (rows 91-100 / 101-110 / 111-120), with three-digit numbers in the squares at the working digit size, and a whole chart of 12 rows. Paper, key and the three screen hosts are one drawing.
teaches: Count, read and write numerals to 120 starting at any number, across 100 (1.NBT.A.1, M.EE.1.NBT.1; lesson G1-Y2.B1 "Count on to 120", design/lessons-first/BUILD_QUEUE.md row 13, QUEUE `G1|-|countonto120`). The chart's two patterns: along a row one more, down a column ten more (1.NBT.C.5 in use). number_chart_fill: the same window on the chart of the hundreds and thousands (101-200 ... 5,001-10,000; 2.NBT.A.2 / 4.NBT.A.2 counting within 1,000 and beyond); it never crosses 100 (its first band starts at 101).
research: No premium logins this round. From knowledge of the reference sites: MathWorksheets4Kids '120 chart' pages (missing numbers on a whole 120 chart, partially filled 120 charts, chart puzzle pieces), K5 Learning grade 1 'counting to 120' and 'missing numbers 1-120' worksheets (fill the missing numbers in a sequence and on chart pieces), IXL grade 1 'Number lines and charts - up to 120' (fill in the missing number on a hundred / 120 chart piece; what number comes after, count forward from a number across 100). Repo sources: PEDAGOGY_STANDARD L-11 ('To 120' sliding windows, the second side a 120 chart with 1 more / 1 less / 10 more / 10 less prompts), design/PROBLEM_TYPES.md CC-15, CC-16, RL-11, GAP-2-06, WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD SP-11a / SP-12a (the 10-column chart on screen). The sites deal 8-30 blanks on one dense whole chart; we keep the window (a page of 4-6 windows, 1-3 squares each) and the whole chart as one cell to a page, as the design standard sets.
problemTypes: Fill the window 95-115 (band 120): a 3 x 5 window cut from rows 91-100, 101-110, 111-120, any five columns; 1 to 3 empty squares dealt (Empty boxes 1-7 when chosen), each with a printed number beside it in its row or column.

What comes after 109? (band 120): a scatter gap at 110 or 111 with 109 / 110 printed on its left; the pupil writes the number after, crossing the decade. The dealer biases band-120 gaps so at least one item in three sits at 100, 101, 110 or 111 (the crossings).

Count on from 98 (band 120): the run along a row (gaps=row) inside rows 91-120, a printed number at each end; counting on ACROSS the row break (98, 99, 100, 101 on one line) is not a chart task: it is `counting:number_seq_fill`, the lesson's other skill.
Fill the row 111-120 (band 120, grid=rows): three whole rows of ten (91-120), a run of up to 8 empty squares along the bottom row, 111 and 120 printed (the run keeps one square in from each edge).
Whole chart (grid=whole, band 120): the 1-120 chart, 12 rows of ten, one cell to a page, gaps scattered / a row / a column / every other square.
Bands below 120 (10 ... 100) and number_chart_fill (101-200 ... 5,001-10,000) unchanged: the same window, the same gap rules.
progression: O2 number size: band 100 (the 1-100 chart) -> band 120 (the window across 100). The build list's '90-110 -> 100-120' rung is the dealer's position inside band 120, not a second band (open question 2).

O3 support: gaps scattered with a printed neighbour on every side it can have one -> a run along a row (count on by 1 from the printed number at its left end) -> a run down a column (count on by 10 from the number above). The row's start stays printed (open question 3).
O6 appearance: a window (3 x 5) -> three whole rows of ten -> the whole chart (one cell to a page).
One change a step (P-1): the band changes the numbers only; the window, the gap rules and the response (write the number in the square) stay.

drawing.sizes: Window squares, band 100 and below: 15 / 16 / 17 mm square (S / M / L). Band 120 (widest number 120, three digits): cellW = max(size width, ceil(3 x 0.56 em x digit pt x 0.8 + 4 mm)) = 15 / 16 / 18 mm wide x 15 / 16 / 17 mm tall, digits at 12.8 / 17.6 / 22.4 pt (0.8 of 16 / 22 / 28, never shrunk, TY-10); a 3 x 5 window is 75 / 80 / 90 mm wide, so two windows share a row at every size (footprint wMm 93, maxCols 2 at L: 90 mm is on the limit, the builder measures it). Empty square border 1.5 pt, printed squares 0.75 pt. Rows of ten at band 120: 10 x 15 / 16 / 18 = 150 / 160 / 180 mm, one to a row. Whole chart 1-120: squares 17.5 mm wide at the L digit size (22.4 pt) at every size; height min(19.5, 195 / rows) = 16.25 mm at 12 rows (195 mm, the same page height the 10-row chart uses), never under 14 mm (H9).
notes: Payload unchanged: {rows (0-based chart rows; 9, 10, 11 = 91-100, 101-110, 111-120), cols, blanks (reading order)}. The template already reads rows past 9; only `cellW` (topOf > 100 widens) and the whole-chart height change. `chart_120` adds no new template (build-list newTemplates: []).
Band 120 window: always rows 9-11 (91-120), so every window crosses 100; c0 dealt 0-5 as today. grid=rows: rows 9-11, all ten columns. grid=whole: rows 0-11 (1-120).

Gap rules unchanged and kept on every band: every gap has a printed number beside it in its row or column; no two scattered gaps side by side in a row; a run stays one square in from each edge. At band 120 the dealer must still put the crossing squares (100, 101, 110, 111) in play: a predicate in ws-options-verify reads 50 items and fails if none is dealt.

Three-digit numbers: 100-120 in an 18 mm square at L is 13.3 mm of digits with 2.3 mm clear each side; at S 7.6 mm in a 15 mm square. The widening is per WINDOW (the widest number in it), so a band-120 window is one width all through; the 1-100 chart (its one three-digit number is 100) keeps its size width as today.

Whole chart at 12 rows: `WHOLE.h` becomes a function of the rows (19.5 mm to 10 rows, 16.25 mm at 12); one cell to a page; the page footer and the header stay; the builder proves it fits A4 and US Letter in one page (ws-empty-band EB-FOOT, ws-cell-checks).
Key (AK-1, AK-2): the same window with each answer written bold in its own square; values joined ', ' in reading order (`q.ans`).

Screen: every empty square is `data-mq-cell` (its own input). A 3 x 5 window fits the card at 390 / 820 / 1280, the online worksheet and the quiz; a row of ten (grid=rows / whole, band 10) stays one row of ten and swipes inside its cell on a phone (SP-11a), sized from its digits above a phone (SP-12a: `--mq-chd` 3 at band 120, squares 3 x 0.58 em + 10 px wide).

Title and words follow the band (L6, L28): at band 120 the I Can reads 'I Can find missing numbers on a chart to 120' (not 'a hundreds chart'), chosen from the options when the page asks with no item; the worked steps already read only numbers the window prints.

Distractors (wrongAnswer) at band 120: the new misconception 'writes-ten-ten' (110 written 1010, 101 written 1001, 100 written 1000) joins wrong-row and one-less; reversed-digits stays for two-digit answers only.

ownerRulings.ruling: hundreds_chart_fill "Numbers to" 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 100; a bigger chart as its own skill (number_chart_fill, "Numbers in" 101-200 ... 5,001-10,000). Rows may run past 9; a window past 100 widens its squares to hold the digits at the working size (the digits never shrink).
A 10-column chart on a phone keeps its digit size and its rows of ten and swipes inside its own cell with a visible cue (SP-11a); above a phone it is sized from its digits (SP-12a).

A distinct option is ALSO a findable skill when it is a distinct new difficulty or skill (a harder size class, a new task kind); small tweaks stay plain options. chart_120 is checked against this rule in open question 1.

options: band (hundreds_chart_fill): add the value 120, label '120 (91 to 120, across 100)', default stays 100 so old pages and share codes are unchanged; the share code of the band option already carries numeric values (ws-code-snapshot must show no MOVED / DELETED line).
Preset skill for band 120: see open question 1 (recommended yes: `composing:chart_to_120`, 'Count to 120 on the Chart', grade 1, 1.NBT.A.1 / M.EE.1.NBT.1, opens hundreds_chart_fill with band 120).
No new grid, gaps or tiles values: band 120 uses the existing ones (open question 3).

Out of scope of this card: the other build-list entries on this template (`bonds_100`, `multiples_2_5_10`, `vis_chart_shade`) are decided on their own cards or an amendment of this one; this card signs the template as it stands plus `chart_120`.

openQuestions.q: Owner rule 2026-10-17: is band 120 a distinct difficulty that must ALSO be a findable preset skill? The build list says preset: false; the lead leans plain option.
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, make the preset `composing:chart_to_120` ('Count to 120 on the Chart'): the rule names 'a harder size class' as its own skill, band 120 teaches a new thing (three-digit numerals and the crossing at 100, the '120' clause of 1.NBT.A.1), it has its own lesson (Count on to 120) and teachers search '120 chart'. If the owner prefers the lead's lean, it stays a plain band value and only search terms on hundreds_chart_fill name 120.

openQuestions.q: Band 120 window rows: always 91-100 / 101-110 / 111-120 (every window crosses 100), or also 81-110 (the '90-110' rung of the build-list ladder)?
openQuestions.recommended: Always rows 91-120: one band, one place, every item practises the crossing; the 90-110 rung is the column position inside that window, not a second band value.

openQuestions.q: The build-list ladder fades 'row starts given -> none' and asks for 'fill the row 111-120'. Add a gaps value that empties a whole row (111 printed nowhere)?
openQuestions.recommended: No new value: the run along a row keeps a printed number at each end (the gap rule every band keeps), so 'fill the row' is grid=rows + gaps=row + Empty boxes 7 (112-119 with 111 and 120 printed). A whole empty row is a later rung if the lesson critic asks for it.

openQuestions.q: WRM tag: build-list chart_120 names Y2.B1.S5, which is 'Partition numbers to 100' (1.NBT.B.2), not counting to 120. WRM has no 'to 120' step. Which tag?
openQuestions.recommended: Fix the build-list entry: tag {step: Y1.B12.S1 'Count from 50 to 100', partial} and keep the lesson link G1-Y2.B1 (Count on to 120) in data/curriculum/links; drop Y2.B1.S5.

openQuestions.q: The whole chart at 120 is 12 rows. Shorter squares (16.25 mm tall, same 17.5 mm width and digit size) to keep one page, or two pages (1-60, 61-120)?
openQuestions.recommended: Shorter squares on one page: the chart's point is the whole pattern in one view, and 16.25 mm stays above the 14 mm writing floor (H9).
